description: Self-declared AI-built application corpus -- fis's ACTUAL TARGET CLASS. Every other corpus in this benchmark (corpus.clean.json, corpus.app.json, corpus.vuln.json, corpus.messy.json) is mature, professionally-maintained open-source software; none of them are the young, AI-scaffolded, often-first-time-builder applications fis is marketed to audit. This corpus fills that gap with 10 repositories whose own README/description SELF-DECLARES AI-tool authorship (Lovable, v0.dev, Claude Code, Bolt.new, or a generic 'vibe coded' claim) -- application-shaped real code (all >30 files, none are libraries, awesome-lists, or prompt/template collections), created within roughly the last 18 months.
ground_truth_caveat: There is NO vulnerability ground truth here and NO expectation of a particular verdict -- this is explicitly field mode, the same no-label semantics as corpus.messy.json. 'Self-declared AI-built' is an AUTHORSHIP label sourced from each repo's own README/badge/description, not a security label. Do not compute or cite an FCR, a recall rate, or a miss/catch count against this corpus -- those metrics require a known-clean or known-vulnerable label, which this corpus does not have and does not claim to have. What this corpus DOES support: (1) qualitative field-behavior reads (are verdicts, scores, and findings proportionate on genuinely AI-scaffolded code, the way corpus.messy.json checks proportionality on large accreted legacy code), and (2) validation of the ai_generated_likelihood signal specifically, since every entry carries an independent, out-of-band authorship label (the tool's own badge/README claim) that the model's ai_generated_likelihood score can be checked against without fis having produced the label itself.
selection_criteria: Each entry: (1) self-declares AI-tool authorship in its own README, description, or topics -- the exact quoted evidence is recorded per entry below; (2) is application-shaped -- a runnable app with real code, not a library/framework/CLI tool (that is corpus.clean.json's job) and not an awesome-list/prompt-collection/meta-tooling repo (excluded a large number of these during search -- topics like `lovable`/`vibe-coding`/`bolt.new` return mostly curated-list and AI-tool-building-tool repos, which were filtered out); (3) has more than 30 files in its git tree (verified live via the GitHub trees API, recorded per entry); (4) was created within roughly the last 18 months (verified live via the GitHub repos API); (5) is publicly fetchable, not a fork, not archived (verified live via the GitHub repos API, 2026-08-11); (6) does not appear in corpus.clean.json, corpus.app.json, corpus.vuln.json, or corpus.messy.json (checked against all four). Language skew toward TypeScript/JavaScript is expected and disclosed, not curated away -- it reflects what Lovable, v0.dev, and Bolt.new actually emit (React/Next.js scaffolds), not a selection choice.
